turns.speaker: SURGEON
turns.text: Let's do our time out. Confirming patient, laparoscopic cholecystectomy, possible conversion to open, consent signed, antibiotics given?

turns.speaker: ANESTHESIA

turns.speaker: SURGEON
turns.text: Great. Everyone agree? Time out complete.

turns.speaker: SURGEON

turns.speaker: SURGEON

turns.speaker: SURGEON
turns.text: Camera's in. There's a lot of inflammation around the gallbladder, omentum is stuck to it. Adhesions are dense.

turns.speaker: SURGEON
turns.text: Taking down the adhesions. The tissue planes are really hard to see here.

turns.speaker: SURGEON
turns.text: I'm having trouble getting a critical view of safety. The anatomy at the triangle is completely obscured.

turns.speaker: SURGEON
turns.text: There's bleeding from the liver bed, more than I'd like. Suction please. Estimate maybe 150 mils so far.

turns.speaker: SURGEON
turns.text: I'm not comfortable continuing laparoscopically. We're going to convert to open. Let's get the open tray.

turns.speaker: ANESTHESIA

turns.speaker: SURGEON

handoff.text:
**I — Illness severity**: watcher
**P — Patient summary**: 54-year-old, laparoscopic cholecystectomy converted to open due to dense adhesions and inability to obtain critical view of safety. Intraoperative hypotension (92/55) and tachycardia (104) during liver bed oozing, resolved with 1L crystalloid. EBL 400 mL. No transfusions. Lines: IV left forearm. Drains: Jackson-Pratt in gallbladder fossa. Implants: none. Counts: correct.
**A — Action list**: Admit to floor overnight for pain control and drain monitoring. Monitor Jackson-Pratt output.
**S — Situation awareness & contingencies**: If drain output increases or becomes bilious, notify surgery. If hemodynamic instability recurs, reassess for bleeding.
**S — Synthesis by receiver**:
Receiver read-back:

opnote.text:
Preoperative diagnosis: acute cholecystitis
Postoperative diagnosis: acute cholecystitis
Procedure: laparoscopic cholecystectomy converted to open cholecystectomy
Surgeon / anesthesia: not documented
Anesthesia type: general endotracheal
Findings: dense adhesions and obscured anatomy preventing critical view of safety
Implants: none documented
Estimated blood loss: 400 mL
Specimens: Gallbladder, acute cholecystitis
Complications: dense adhesions and obscured anatomy preventing critical view of safety; converted to open due to inability to obtain critical view of safety; hypotension (92/55) and tachycardia (104) during liver bed oozing
Counts: correct
Disposition: floor (PACU first, then admitted overnight to floor for pain control and drain monitoring)
Brief narrative: The patient underwent induction with propofol and rocuronium for a planned laparoscopic cholecystectomy. During dissection, dense adhesions and obscured anatomy prevented the surgeon from obtaining a critical view of safety, prompting conversion to an open procedure via a right subcostal incision. The gallbladder was removed and sent to pathology, and a Jackson-Pratt drain was placed in the gallbladder fossa. The patient experienced transient hypotension and tachycardia during liver bed oozing, which resolved after a 1L crystalloid bolus. The procedure concluded with correct counts and closure, and the patient was admitted to the floor for pain control and drain monitoring.

family.text: Your family member had surgery to remove their gallbladder because of severe inflammation. The team started with small incisions, but there was a difficulty during the procedure where the anatomy was hard to see safely, so the surgeon made a larger incision to finish the operation carefully. The surgery is complete, and the team is taking good care of them to manage pain and monitor a small drain left in place. They are not in critical condition, but they will spend the night in the hospital for close observation. You can expect to see them in the recovery area soon, and they will be moved to a regular hospital room afterward. The surgeon will come speak with you directly.

A 3.0 x 18 mm drug-eluting stent was deployed in the mid LAD, followed by post-dilation with a 3.5 non-compliant balloon. The procedure concluded with the removal of the sheath, application of a radial band, and transfer to the CCU for overnight monitoring.

handoff.text:
**I — Illness severity**: stable
No complications documented. Hemodynamics not documented.

**P — Patient summary**: Robotic-assisted total knee arthroplasty (Mako system). Intraoperative course included equipment troubleshooting (camera connection, missing 6mm frame, missing corn solution/pomade). Tibial and femoral components implanted with bone cement. Counts correct. Phase reached: closure.

**A — Action list**: 
- Monitor for standard post-operative recovery.
- No specific follow-up actions documented beyond standard closure care.

**S — Situation awareness & contingencies**: 
- Equipment issues resolved intraoperatively; no ongoing technical contingencies.
- No open concerns documented.
- If/then: Not documented.

**S — Synthesis by receiver**: 
Receiver read-back:

Surgeon / anesthesia: not documented

Brief narrative: The procedure began with troubleshooting a camera connection error on the robotic system. After setup and registration of the Mako system, a timeout was performed to confirm the left side. The surgeon then proceeded with the key procedure, placing a small tibial component and subsequently a femoral component. Bone cement was administered intraosseously during the implantation process. The case concluded with the transition to the closure phase.

family.text: Your loved one is currently in the final stages of their knee replacement surgery. The surgical team successfully placed the new bone components and is now closing the incision. There were no serious medical complications during the procedure, and the team is taking good care of them. The patient will move to the recovery area to wake up from anesthesia. The surgeon will come speak with you directly.
